title: Bechorot daf 61

chapters.title: Simultaneous Animals in the Tenth Slot
chapters.about: Rav Kahana and Rav Ashi on two animals emerging together at the tenth count.

chapters.title: Uprooting the Tenth Animal's Name
chapters.about: Analyzing the Mishna rule regarding uprooting the status of the tenth animal.

chapters.title: Rabbi's View on Calling Ten Eleven
chapters.about: Debating whether calling the tenth animal eleventh constitutes uprooting.

chapters.title: Rulings on Simultaneous Tenth Animals
chapters.about: Differing opinions of Hakhamim, Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Yehuda on simultaneous animals.

chapters.title: Ma'aser Behemah Nowadays
chapters.about: Concerns over stumbling blocks (takala) in modern times regarding tithed animals.

chapters.title: Counting Errors Made by an Agent
chapters.about: Disagreement between Rav Pepi and Rav Papa on whether an agent's tithing error takes effect.

chapters.title: Siyum Bechorot and Beginning Masekhet Arakhin
chapters.about: Completing Masekhet Bechorot and reading the first Mishna in Arakhin regarding valuation vows.

summary: This class concludes Masekhet Bechorot by analyzing the laws of animal tithes (Ma'aser Behemah), focusing on cases where animals emerge simultaneously or are miscounted during the tithing process. It examines whether counting errors made by the owner or an appointed agent (shaliah) alter the sacred status of the animals, as well as rabbinic decrees applied nowadays. The lesson finishes with a celebration of the siyum and introduces the opening Mishna of Masekhet Arakhin concerning personal valuation vows.
subjects: Uprooting the tenth animal status (Ne'ekar shem asiri)
Opinions of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
questions: What is the status of animals when two emerge simultaneously in the tenth slot during tithing?
Does calling the tenth animal 'eleventh' uproot its status as the tenth animal?
Why are tithed animals nowadays left to die rather than left to graze?
Does an agent's counting error invalidate the tithe on behalf of the owner?
Who is eligible to make or be the subject of an Erekh valuation vow?
